_comment: THE mbiXaddin CONFIGURATION CONTRACT — what its C# accepts.
TODAY THIS FILE IS HAND-WRITTEN, and that is a temporary state with a plan:
mbiXaddin gains a test that reflects over its own enums, writes this file,
and fails when it is stale. Then it publishes it to mbiX-hub, ScrapeX reads
it from there, and nobody transcribes anything ever again.
Until that lands, the honest description is: a snapshot, taken on the date
below, by seven agents reading ~350 .cs files with file:line for every
answer. The full record is docs/reviews/mbiXaddin-config-contract-*.md.
TWO VERSIONS, AND THEY MEAN DIFFERENT THINGS.
contractVersion  — the SHAPE below. Bumped when a vocabulary gains or
loses a value. Mechanically checkable: a generator
rewrites extension/addin-vocabulary.js and a test
fails if the two disagree.
behaviourVersion — how the add-in BEHAVES: what a blank cell means, what
happens to an unknown transform, whether a bad row is
dropped or fails the table. NONE OF THAT IS IN AN ENUM
and none of it can be extracted mechanically. It is a
number a human raises, and raising it fails ScrapeX's
gate on purpose — the Console's rules must then be
re-read from the code before anything ships.
That asymmetry is the point. Behaviour cannot be automated, so instead it
is made impossible to change SILENTLY.
_comment_read_against: WHICH UPSTREAM STATE THIS READING DESCRIBES, as a commit rather than a date,
because a date cannot be checked and a commit can. Everything the Console
believes about mbiXaddin was read from the tree at readAgainstCommit.
IT IS RECORDED BECAUSE THE VERSION NUMBERS ABOVE CANNOT DETECT UPSTREAM
DRIFT. mbiXaddin has no behaviourVersion of its own — both numbers live in
THIS repository, and the same hand raises both in the same commit, so their
agreement proves ScrapeX is internally consistent and nothing more. The
commit is what lets a test go and look: see the file-drift guard in
this reading cites against the add-in's own main branch.
reviewedSince — cited files that HAVE moved since, each read and found not
to touch what the Console believes, pinned to the blob they were dismissed
at. A further edit changes the blob and the guard fires again. THIS LIST IS
EVIDENCE, NOT AN EXEMPTION: an entry with no reason is a hole.

EndpointCatalog.cs.why: A comment rewrite about which release endpoint is still served. The six compiled-in sheet gids the Console refuses a wrong workbook by are untouched.

HttpClientService.cs.why: 5xx backoff bounded by the caller's timeout. Network retry behaviour; it decides nothing about the six configuration sheets.

mbiXRibbon.cs.why: One click throttle and one dialog presenter across five ribbon buttons. UI plumbing, not 6.RibbonControls semantics.

_comment_TABLE_UX_CONFIG_KEYS: The four JSON bags on 1.TableDefinition, read from the C# classes that
back them. A key outside these sets is accepted, kept, and never read —
the add-in warns with a Levenshtein "did you mean", so the Console can
say the same thing while the key is still being typed.
_comment_RIBBON_CONTROL_KEYS: A CLOSED set that is nowhere declared as one: a 6.RibbonControls row
renders only if its CONTROL_KEY equals the Name of a control wired to the
data-driven handler. Twenty-one menus reach mnuDynamic_ItemsLoading
(mbiXRibbon.cs:1099, wired 21x in mbiXRibbon.Designer.cs) and two buttons
are registered with BindButton (mbiXRibbon.cs:261-262). mnuExport is NOT
sheet-driven — it is built by RibbonContentBuilder.
AND THE DEFAULT IS NOT IN THE SET. A blank cell becomes 'mnuDynamic'
(RibbonControlService.cs:513), and NO control of that name exists in the
shipped designer — so a blank CONTROL_KEY renders NOWHERE, with no error
anywhere. That is why the default is recorded beside the set instead of
inside it: it is a trap, not a value.
_comment_LOG_TAGS: Faults the add-in reports ONLY as a bracketed tag on a log line — there is
no ValidationResult and so no error code. The tag is still the string an
owner greps for, so the Console prints it rather than inventing a name.

_comment_uri: SourceUriValidator now parses the URI and compares the normalised HOST
exactly against these two Google Sheets hosts (SourceUriValidator change
merged 2026-08-13, mbiXaddin PR #26). It strips trailing root dots and
compares case-insensitively; userinfo, ports, paths and query strings do
not participate. The TSV and gid literals are still searched in the
whole lower-cased address after that host decision.
